meta.source: Chinese Pediatric Society child-care guidance · AAP (American Academy of Pediatrics) · WHO Child Injury Prevention (reference)
meta.usage: Enforced by the safety filter (§6.3) during menu/games generation; emergency_red_lines are referenced by kid-journal/kid-review anomaly alerting (§6.6).
meta.disclaimer: This rule library provides home care and safety tips only and cannot replace professional medical advice. When any emergency_red_line condition is matched, advise seeking immediate medical care.

emergency_red_lines.condition: Fever >= 38 degrees C (axillary) in an infant under 3 months
emergency_red_lines.action: Seek immediate medical care (emergency/pediatrics); do not give antipyretics on your own

emergency_red_lines.condition: Listlessness, lethargy, hard to wake, or vacant unresponsive gaze
Breathing difficulty, rapid breathing, nasal flaring, chest retractions, or blue lips/face
emergency_red_lines.action: Call emergency services and seek medical care

emergency_red_lines.condition: Seizure/convulsion (eyes rolling up, stiff or rhythmically jerking limbs, loss of consciousness)
emergency_red_lines.action: Place child on their side to prevent aspiration, record duration; seek care immediately after the episode; call emergency services if it lasts over 5 minutes

emergency_red_lines.condition: Signs of dehydration: no tears when crying, dry lips, sunken fontanelle, markedly reduced urine (no wet diaper for 6-8 h in infants)
emergency_red_lines.action: Seek care promptly; give small frequent amounts of oral rehydration solution en route

emergency_red_lines.condition: Persistent vomiting (>= 3 episodes in 24 h) or projectile vomiting
Anterior fontanelle markedly bulging and tense (remains full/bulging when calm and upright)
Persistent high fever: >= 39 degrees C for more than 24 h, or any fever over 3 days without improvement
emergency_red_lines.action: See a doctor within 24 h; return promptly if fever persists 3 days

emergency_red_lines.condition: Pale, mottled, or marbled skin, or petechiae/bruising that does not blanch on pressure
Suspected ingestion of medicine/cleaner/poison, or choking/aspiration on a foreign object (persistent coughing, stridor, color change)
emergency_red_lines.action: Call emergency services immediately; for choking perform age-appropriate back blows and chest thrusts (Heimlich for children); do not blindly sweep the throat; bring the product packaging to the hospital

emergency_red_lines.condition: Loss of consciousness, or vomiting, drowsiness, unsteady gait, or unequal pupils after head injury
emergency_red_lines.action: Call emergency services and seek care; avoid shaking the head during transport

emergency_red_lines.condition: Severe abdominal pain lasting over 2 h with refusal to be touched, or bloody/black/current-jelly stools
emergency_red_lines.action: Seek immediate medical care (beware intussusception and other acute abdomen)

emergency_red_lines.condition: Markedly reduced urine or no urination for 12+ h, with eyelid swelling or tea-colored urine
Loss of previously mastered skills at any age (stops walking, loses words)
emergency_red_lines.action: Arrange a developmental/pediatric neurology assessment promptly

under_3_years_forbidden: Whole nuts (peanuts, sunflower seeds, cashews, etc.)
Jelly cups (especially mini-cup jelly; not for toddlers in any form)
Whole pitted/stoned dates; large chunks of fruit with pits
Round sausage slices, large marshmallows, sticky rice cakes/mochi
preparation: Cut grapes and cherry tomatoes into quarters
Remove all bones and fine fishbones from fish
Cut meat into small pieces (<=1.5 cm) or strips/mince
Grind nuts; grate apples or cut into thin slices
Pit dates and cut into strips; cut round foods (carrots, banana) lengthwise, never into round coin slices
Children eat seated upright with an adult present; no feeding while running, jumping, laughing, or lying down

principles: No self-medication for children: before any medicine (including OTC drugs, traditional remedies, supplements), follow a doctor's advice or read the pediatric dosing table carefully and calculate by weight
Aspirin is prohibited in children (Reye syndrome risk); for fever use acetaminophen (>= 2-3 months) or ibuprofen (>= 6 months), with intervals and doses per label/doctor
No antibiotic misuse: antibiotics are ineffective against viral colds, require a prescription and full course; never stop early or save leftovers
Giving reduced adult doses to children is dangerous and prohibited
Never stack antipyretics (different brand names may both be acetaminophen); avoid compound cold medicines containing the same ingredient while dosing fever medicine
Store medicines, vitamins, and cleaners in a locked cabinet out of children's reach; keep original packaging and dosing devices; dispose of expired medicines
Do not mix medicine into a full bottle of milk or trick children with 'candy'

risks: Soft bedding and bumpers in crib (suffocation)
preventions: Crib bar spacing <= 6 cm (standard 2.5-6 cm)
Tie curtain cords high (>1.2 m) or replace with cordless styles
For the first year, crib holds only the baby and a fitted sheet; use sleep sacks instead of blankets
Anchor tall furniture to the wall with anti-tip brackets; add child locks to drawers

risks: Head impact on table corners and edges
Small parts swallowed (button batteries, coins, magnetic balls)
preventions: Outlet covers; prefer outlets with built-in shutters for unused positions
Corner guards on tables; keep heavy objects away from table edges (against pull-down)
Store button batteries, magnetic balls, coins, and pins out of reach; button battery ingestion is an emergency requiring immediate care
Route cables along walls; place appliances against the wall

risks: Scalds from hot soup, water, and oil
preventions: Turn pot handles inward; keep hot drinks on the inner side of counters; no tablecloths (pull-over hazard)
Lock knives in a drawer; sweep and discard broken glass immediately
Keep cleaners in original packaging (never in drink bottles) in a locked cabinet; never mix bleach with toilet cleaner (chlorine gas)
Close the gas valve after use; knob guards; install a gas alarm

risks: Drowning (as little as 5 cm of water can drown an infant)
preventions: Never leave an infant/toddler unattended in a tub or bucket — not even to answer the phone; empty buckets and basins after use
Non-slip mats in bathroom; anti-slip stickers in tub
Run cold water first, then hot; confirm 37-38 degrees C with a thermometer; water heater set <= 49 degrees C
Lock away razors, medicines, and cosmetics; toilet seat lock

risks: Falls from windows and balcony railings
Head entrapment or passage between railings
preventions: Window limiters (opening <= 10 cm) or safety netting; no climbable furniture/boxes near windows
Balcony railing spacing <= 11 cm, height >= 1.1 m; nothing stacked to climb; child lock on balcony door
Safety gates at top and bottom of stairs; avoid horizontal climbable rails

risks: Child left alone at home / in a car
preventions: Keep matches and lighters out of reach; install smoke alarms and test every 6 months
Never leave children alone with pets; teach not to disturb feeding/sleeping animals; wash bites with soap and water and seek care for rabies evaluation
Never leave a child alone at home or in a car under any circumstance (a locked car can become fatal within minutes)

screen_time.under_18m: Avoid screens (video calls excepted); babies under 18 months need live human interaction; avoid background TV
screen_time.18-24m: If introduced: high-quality content only, co-viewed and narrated by a caregiver, < 1 h/day split into short sessions
screen_time.2-5y: < 1 h/day; preview content; co-view and connect to real life; no screens 1 h before meals and bedtime
screen_time.6-12y: Agree on daily limits and content together (family media plan); must not harm sleep (screens off 1 h before bed), physical activity (>= 60 min moderate-to-vigorous daily), or homework; screens out of bedroom and mealtimes; mind content ratings and online safety
